tagline: Eastern Seaboard gateway — marina depth + island day-trip volume near Bangkok.
summary: Pattaya sits about two hours by road southeast of Bangkok on the Eastern Seaboard, anchored by Ocean Marina — the largest marina in Southeast Asia — and fed by a heavy daily flow of day-trippers to Koh Larn. As the closest big-water playground to the capital, it draws on a Chonburi visitor base of more than eleven million arrivals a year, blending domestic weekenders, international tourists and Eastern Economic Corridor business travel. That mix of deep marine infrastructure, premium willingness-to-pay and a short, proven island corridor makes Pattaya the natural Gulf-gateway complement to Bangkok: the place to prove out premium coastal and island-transfer service before extending the network down the coast.

use_cases.title: Pattaya ↔ Koh Larn premium island transfer
use_cases.body: A fast, smooth foiling hop from Bali Hai Pier to Koh Larn that skips the crowded, noisy speedboat scrum. For Bangkok weekenders it turns the island crossing into the calm, premium start of the day rather than a wet, queued ordeal.

use_cases.title: Marina-based charter & premium transfers
use_cases.body: Operating out of Ocean Marina — Southeast Asia's largest — a foiling fleet runs on-demand coastal charters and resort transfers with ready berthing and shore charging on site. The marina's yachting clientele is exactly the audience that pays for a silent, signature on-water experience.

use_cases.title: Eastern Seaboard coastal shuttle
use_cases.body: A premium coastal link along the Eastern Seaboard connecting Pattaya, the marina and nearby beach nodes, with land handoff toward Bangkok and the EEC. It gives business and leisure travellers a fast water alternative to congested coastal roads.

journeys.today: Shared diesel speedboat or slow ferry, ~30-40 min, crowded pier and queues at peak.
journeys.with_navier: A fast, smooth foiling hop on demand — quiet, dry and clear of the pier scrum.

journeys.today: Charter speedboats and tenders; no scheduled premium electric link.
journeys.with_navier: A marina-anchored foiling shuttle with berthing and charging on site, gliding to the coastal nodes.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pattaya's corridors are all short and sheltered — Bali Hai↔Koh Larn (~5 nm) and the Ocean Marina coastal hops (~6 nm) — sitting comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, with Ocean Marina's 455 berths giving the best ready-made charging and berthing base in the new cluster.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, opens longer Eastern Seaboard and cross-Gulf runs from the marina — toward Koh Samet, Sattahip and beyond — without relying on shore power at smaller coastal nodes.

competitive_landscape: Conventional speedboats and ferries to Koh Larn; no premium electric option. Ocean Marina serves charters but not scheduled transfer.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Mar cool season. Gulf is relatively sheltered here vs open Gulf islands — broader operating window.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Marine Department licensing; Chonburi/EEC special economic zone may offer a pilot-friendly regulatory environment.
